1. Lack of Patient-Context Awareness: Most medical chatbot systems provide generic responses without considering individual patient profiles including allergies, medications, and vital signs.
2. Cloud Dependency: Nearly all existing medical AI systems require constant internet connectivity, making them unusable in rural and underserved areas with poor network access.
3. Siloed Functionality: Medical imaging, text-based QA, and report digitization typically exist as separate systems with no unified workflow.
4. Limited Personalization: Existing RAG systems retrieve medical knowledge effectively but do not use patient-specific data to condition the generation process.
5. No Safety Mechanisms: Most medical chatbots lack built-in safety checks for allergy warnings, drug interaction alerts, or emergency symptom detection.
6. Poor Report Digitization: Paper-based medical reports remain difficult to convert into structured digital formats, and most OCR pipelines stop at raw text extraction.

7. No Offline Data Persistence: Few healthcare AI applications implement offline data persistence, meaning diagnostic history, chat transcripts, and vital signs are lost during connectivity disruption
8. Black-Box Models: Many medical AI systems lack transparency in their reasoning process, making it difficult for healthcare professionals to trust or verify the outputs.
9. Limited Multi-Modal Integration: Systems that combine text reasoning, image analysis, and document processing within a single deployable platform remain rare.
10. Scalability Concerns: Many prototype systems are designed for demonstration only and lack the architectural robustness needed for real-world clinical deployment.
1. To develop a context-aware personalized medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation system that conditions generation on both structured patient information and retrieved clinical literature.
2. To integrate textual reasoning with CNN-driven chest X-ray classification and OCR-assisted report structuring inside a unified platform.
3. To implement an offline-first PWA design leveraging IndexedDB together with service-worker caching to handle intermittent connectivity in resource-limited environments.
4. To introduce a safety-oriented response flagging mechanism that highlights allergies, drug interactions, and emergency symptoms in generated medical advice.
5. To develop a ResNet101-based CNN model for five-class chest X-ray categorization with clinically meaningful severity labels and confidence scores.
6. To implement an OCR pipeline using EasyOCR combined with LLM-based zero-shot extraction for converting paper medical reports into structured digital records.
7. To design role-based patient and doctor dashboards with comprehensive health overview, medical timeline, and AI diagnostic capabilities.
8. To evaluate the system’s performance using standard metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix analysis.
9. To study and analyze existing medical AI systems through a detailed literature survey to identify limitations and research gaps.
10. To develop a scalable three-tier architecture that can be extended for future applications such as FHIR interoperability, federated learning, and multilingual support.

•  Accuracy: The ResNet101 model achieved approximately 84% accuracy on the test partition, demonstrating strong performance in classifying chest X-rays across five disease categories.

Although the system performs well, several improvements can be made to enhance its capabilities:
1. FHIR-Compatible Interoperability: Implement Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources standards to enable seamless exchange with hospital information systems.
2. Federated Learning: Investigate federated learning approaches to refine the imaging model across multiple institutions without centralizing sensitive patient data.
3. Multilingual Support: Add multilingual prompting and support for regional medical vocabularies to broaden accessibility across diverse linguistic communities.
4. Wearable Integration: Develop native integration with smartwatches and wearable devices for real-time vital sign streaming into the patient context.
5. Enhanced OCR: Improve the OCR pipeline to handle handwritten prescriptions, multilingual documents, and low-quality scans with higher accuracy.
6. Video Consultation: Integrate telemedicine capabilities for direct doctor-patient video consultations within the platform.
